input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unconditional election to terminate the Agreement by written notice, with services running only to the last day of the month following the month of notice — i.e. an effective notice period of no more than about 60 days, which is at or better than the fallback's 60–90 day window (the mechanic is month-end rather than a flat 30 days, so it is short of the preferred wording only in that minor respect). No early-termination fee, exit charge or penalty exists anywhere: Section 5a (p0045) bills Hosting and Support Services monthly with invoices paid within 15 days of receipt, so fees are payable in arrears and there are no prepaid fees to refund; the absence of any termination charge is better than the fallback's three-months-of-fees cap. TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right: the only TrueLink-side exits in Section 13 (p0078) are (i) partial termination of Sections 2 and 3 triggered by Client breach/default consequences, which is a for-cause mechanic, and (ii) notice of intent not to renew at the end of an annual term, which is natural-term non-renewal and belongs under the RENEWAL rule rather than T4C (TrueLink's 30-day non-renewal notice falls short of a 90-day preference, but I do not flag it here to avoid double-counting the same term). The initial term is one year with annual auto-renewal, so this is not a multi-year commitment without a Customer exit and walk-away territory is not engaged. The clause therefore meets every fallback element on its material terms and I do not redline it merely to reach the preferred 30-day/pro-rata refund formulation.
